summary: In the ABFAB architecture, this standards-track RFC describes using SAML with RADIUS. It defines two RADIUS attributes, a SAML binding, a name identifier format, two profiles and two confirmation methods, so SAML assertions and protocol messages can be carried inside RADIUS.

eli5.summary: SAML is a note vouching for who you are. This lets that note travel inside RADIUS, a system already used to check logins.

questions: what are the saml-assertion and saml-protocol radius attributes
what is the abfab authentication profile
how does saml work with radius
subtitle: Carries SAML assertions and messages inside RADIUS so federated identity can reach beyond the web.

tldr.problem: SAML normally travels over HTTP-based bindings meant for web single sign-on, but the ABFAB architecture wants federated identity for non-web applications built on the AAA framework.
tldr.mechanism: Two RADIUS attributes (SAML-Assertion and SAML-Protocol) wrap SAML content, and a SAML RADIUS binding, two profiles, a NAI name identifier format and two confirmation methods define how a Relying Party and Identity Provider use them.
tldr.outcome: A Relying Party acting as a RADIUS client can ask an Identity Provider acting as a RADIUS server to authenticate a client, or to answer assertion queries, with the answer carried in RADIUS messages. The artifacts are not exclusive to ABFAB.

today: RFC 7833 is a Standards Track document, and the metadata for this entry lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on the ABFAB architecture of RFC 7831.

sections.title: Why SAML Needs RADIUS
sections.content:
Within the ABFAB (Application Bridging for Federated Access Beyond web) architecture of RFC 7831, it is often desirable to convey Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) assertions and protocol messages. SAML typically considers only HTTP-based transports, called bindings, which are mainly intended for the SAML V2.0 web browser single sign-on profile.

ABFAB aims to extend federated identity to other applications by building on the Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting (AAA) framework. So SAML must integrate with AAA protocols such as RADIUS (RFC 2865) and Diameter (RFC 6733), as well as HTTP. This document defines:

  • two RADIUS attributes that encapsulate SAML assertions and protocol messages
  • a SAML RADIUS binding
  • a name identifier format based on the Network Access Identifier (NAI)
  • a profile of the SAML Authentication Request Protocol and a profile of the Assertion Query and Request Protocol
  • two subject confirmation methods
sections.eli5: Normally the signed identity note travels by web. Here it is taught to travel by another route, the one login systems already use.

sections.title: Three Vocabularies for the Same Roles
sections.content:
SAML, RADIUS and ABFAB name the same parties differently, and the RFC prefers the ABFAB term. The mapping in its Table 1:

  • Client (ABFAB): called Subject or Principal in SAML, and User in RADIUS.
  • Relying Party (ABFAB): Service Provider or Requester in SAML; NAS or RADIUS client in RADIUS.
  • Identity Provider (ABFAB): Identity Provider, Responder or Issuer in SAML; AS or RADIUS server in RADIUS.

Here NAS means network access server and AS means authentication server.
sections.eli5: The same school, student and teacher are called different names in different books. This table lines the names up.

sections.title: The Two RADIUS Attributes
sections.content:
Because SAML structures are typically large, both attributes use the Long Extended Type format of RFC 6929. Both have Type 245 and a length of at least 5.

  • SAML-Assertion: Extended-Type 1; the value encodes a SAML Assertion.
  • SAML-Protocol: Extended-Type 2; the value encodes a SAML protocol message.

They are exclusive alternatives, so RADIUS entities MUST NOT put both in the same RADIUS message. The M (More) and Reserved fields work as described in RFC 6929.
sections.eli5: There are two kinds of envelope. One holds a finished note, and one holds a question or an answer. You never put both in the same package.

sections.title: The SAML RADIUS Binding
sections.content:
The binding is identified by urn:ietf:params:abfab:bindings:radius. The Relying Party (RP) MUST trust statements in SAML messages from the Identity Provider (IdP) as it trusts RADIUS attributes, and both MUST trust the RADIUS infrastructure for integrity. It is REQUIRED that the exchange be protected with TLS for RADIUS (RFC 6614), unless other means such as IPsec tunnels or a sufficiently secure internal network provide confidentiality and integrity.

There are two system models:

  1. Request and response. The RP, as RADIUS client, sends one SAML request element in an Access-Request using SAML-Protocol. That message MUST carry a single User-Name attribute in NAI form (RFC 7542). The IdP returns one SAML protocol message in an Access-Accept or Access-Reject, which ends the exchange. An IdP that refuses can silently discard the request.
  2. Unsolicited assertion. The IdP puts a single SAML Assertion in the SAML-Assertion attribute of an Access-Accept.

An IdP SHOULD return a RADIUS State attribute in the Access-Accept so later queries can run against the same authentication context. Other RADIUS attributes may be used freely, since the binding is meant to be composed with uses such as network access.

Names matter for policy. IdPs SHOULD apply policy based on the RP's identity tied to the Access-Request, and RPs SHOULD use the NAI realm of the Access-Accept. To use SAML entityIDs, the SAML name must be linked to the AAA name through trusted metadata or a trusted signed message that includes the RADIUS identity. A signature alone is not enough, because a malicious RADIUS entity could copy a SAML message into a different RADIUS message. The RFC extends SAML metadata with RADIUS IdP and RADIUS RP role descriptors for this.
sections.eli5: The school asks the office a question on the login system's own form, and the office answers on the same form. Everyone checks that the form really came from that office.

sections.title: The ABFAB Authentication Profile
sections.content:
The profile urn:ietf:params:abfab:profiles:authentication is a profile of the SAML Authentication Request Protocol and MUST be used with the SAML RADIUS binding. A client using a User Agent asks an RP for access. The RP, as RADIUS client, checks the client's credentials against the RADIUS server acting as its IdP, which, on success, produces an authentication assertion for the RP to consume.

It is based on the SAML web browser single sign-on profile, with differences: no particular authentication method is required (ABFAB itself requires EAP), HTTP bindings are not used, the RP may not name the Subject of the AuthnRequest, and the IdP returns a single message or assertion that MUST contain exactly one authentication statement.

The flow has five steps: the client requests a resource, the RP optionally sends a samlp:AuthnRequest to the IdP, the IdP identifies the client, the IdP sends a samlp:Response, and the RP grants or denies access. If ForceAuthn is true the IdP MUST establish identity afresh rather than reuse session state.

A successful response MUST contain exactly one assertion with a saml:AuthnStatement and a SubjectConfirmation using the confirmation method urn:ietf:params:abfab:cm:user or urn:ietf:params:abfab:cm:machine, meaning the subject is the user or machine authenticated by an earlier Access-Accept, identified by its State attribute. An error response MUST NOT contain assertions. The RP MUST discard invalid assertions and honor SessionNotOnOrAfter. Implementations MUST NOT require XML signatures, but MAY use them.
sections.eli5: You show up at a club. The club asks your school to vouch for you, the school checks who you are and sends one signed note back, and the club lets you in or not.

sections.title: The Assertion Query/Request Profile
sections.content:
The second profile, urn:ietf:params:abfab:profiles:query, applies the SAML RADIUS binding to the SAML V2.0 Assertion Query/Request Profile, which is usually discussed with the SOAP binding. The RP sends an AssertionIDRequest, SubjectQuery, AuthnQuery, AttributeQuery or AuthzDecisionQuery to a SAML authority, which answers with a Response.

Differences from the base profile: the IdP MUST prefer the client identifier implied by the RADIUS State attribute over the one in the SAML request's Subject, and XML signatures MUST NOT be required. The Access-Request MUST include a Service-Type of Authorize-Only, and SHOULD include State when the query concerns a previously authenticated client. TLS protection is RECOMMENDED.

This is what the two confirmation methods are for: queries about a previously authenticated user or machine need not name the subject explicitly.
sections.eli5: Later, the club can ask the school more questions about you, like your grade. It points to the earlier visit instead of saying your name again.

sections.title: Privacy and Security
sections.content:
IdPs MUST apply policy to decide what is released to each RP. The client's identity is typically hidden from the RP unless the IdP provides it, while the RP usually knows the IdP's realm. Even generic attributes such as affiliation can help identify a client, and some attributes let an RP, or a group of RPs, link the same client across sessions. The profiles give clients no direct way to state preferences, which can be handled out of band, such as at enrollment.

If RADIUS proxies are used without encryption, they can see the attributes the IdP discloses, which the RFC calls a significant privacy exposure in some deployments. Passive eavesdroppers can read assertions without TLS, so TLS is strongly encouraged.

For security, the RP MUST filter information according to what the IdP may assert and how far proxies can be trusted. XML signatures and encryption are OPTIONAL end-to-end protection against modification by proxies, and are not mandatory to implement.
sections.eli5: The school should only tell the club what it needs to know. And if the note passes through helpers, they should not be able to read it.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA registered the attributes as 245.1 (SAML-Assertion) and 245.2 (SAML-Protocol) in the RADIUS long extended space. It also created a registry, "Application Bridging for Federated Access Beyond Web (ABFAB) Parameters", with a sub-registry of ABFAB URN Parameters, filled by IETF Review or Expert Review. The initial entries are bindings:radius, nameid-format:nai, profiles:authentication, profiles:query, cm:user and cm:machine. The abfab URN sub-namespace was registered as well.
sections.eli5: The new names were written in an official list so nobody else picks the same ones.

fields.desc: 1 for SAML-Assertion; the SAML-Protocol attribute uses 2.
